tasks.title: Audit one explicit-formula bottleneck
tasks.objective: State one precisely scoped implication from an explicit formula toward the Riemann Hypothesis, identify every analytic hypothesis it uses, and either prove the implication or isolate the first unsupported step.
tasks.rationale: A small dependency with explicit quantifiers is easier to verify and reuse than another end-to-end proof sketch.
tasks.successCriteria: A complete derivation of the scoped implication with all domains, limits, and error terms stated.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A minimal unsupported estimate or interchange of limits, with a concrete condition that would repair it.
tasks.verificationMethod: Line-by-line symbolic checking against the stated hypotheses, plus independent checks of every limiting operation.

tasks.title: Stress-test a critical-strip estimate
tasks.objective: Choose one estimate that would strengthen control of zeta zeros in the critical strip, state its exact range and constants, and test the shortest plausible derivation for a hidden circularity or loss of uniformity.
tasks.rationale: Uniformity and endpoint behavior are common failure points in analytic arguments.
tasks.successCriteria: A checkable estimate in a nontrivial stated range, or a rigorously justified reduction to one named sublemma.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A concrete counterexample to the proposed estimate or a precisely located nonuniform step.
tasks.verificationMethod: Re-derive the inequalities independently and test edge cases using exact or interval-safe calculations where applicable.

tasks.title: Design an off-line zero certificate
tasks.objective: Specify the smallest independently checkable certificate that would rigorously establish a nontrivial zeta zero off the critical line, including error bounds, multiplicity handling, and a verifier contract.
tasks.rationale: A search is scientifically useful only if a candidate can be certified without trusting floating-point output.
tasks.successCriteria: A complete certificate format and deterministic verification procedure with explicit numerical error requirements.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A precise explanation of which certification step remains unavailable and what additional bound is required.
tasks.verificationMethod: Audit the verifier specification for exactness and test it on synthetic near-zero and on-line cases.

tasks.title: Prove a safe zero-search pruning rule
tasks.objective: Formulate one mathematically safe rule for excluding a bounded region from an off-line-zero search, and prove that the rule cannot discard a genuine counterexample within its declared scope.
tasks.rationale: Certified pruning can compound across searches without turning a finite negative result into a global claim.
tasks.successCriteria: A proved pruning lemma with an executable or hand-checkable certificate for one bounded region.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A smallest case showing that the proposed pruning rule is unsound or too weak to save work.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent proof review and adversarial tests at all boundary cases.

tasks.title: Audit one candidate algorithm invariant
tasks.objective: Take one proposed polynomial-time strategy for an NP-complete problem, state the invariant on which its runtime or correctness depends, and try to prove or minimally falsify that invariant.
tasks.rationale: Most candidate algorithms fail at a compact invariant or worst-case family that can be preserved as reusable evidence.
tasks.successCriteria: A proof of the invariant and its polynomial bound on the declared input model.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A minimal adversarial instance family that breaks correctness, progress, or the claimed runtime.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent asymptotic analysis and exact execution on a generated adversarial family when code is used.

tasks.title: Formalize a reduction-to-algorithm interface
tasks.objective: Choose one standard NP-complete reduction relevant to a candidate algorithm, formalize its input-size and witness-preservation guarantees, and test whether the algorithm's promised bound survives the reduction.
tasks.rationale: Hidden encoding growth can invalidate otherwise plausible polynomial-time claims.
tasks.successCriteria: A complete size-preserving interface proof with explicit encodings and complexity parameters.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A precise encoding or promise mismatch that blocks composition.
tasks.verificationMethod: Check every size transformation and quantify the composed runtime independently.

tasks.title: Isolate a restricted-model lower-bound lemma
tasks.objective: State one nontrivial lower-bound lemma in a clearly restricted computational model, prove as much as possible, and mark exactly why the argument does or does not extend toward general polynomial time.
tasks.rationale: Restricted results are reusable only when the boundary of the model is explicit.
tasks.successCriteria: A complete lower-bound proof in the declared model with an explicit extension barrier.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A concrete construction defeating the proposed measure or induction.
tasks.verificationMethod: Reconstruct the proof from definitions and test the complexity measure on edge-case circuits or machines.

tasks.title: Classify one proof idea against known barriers
tasks.objective: Express one proposed P versus NP separation technique as an explicit proof schema and determine, with stated assumptions, whether relativization, natural-proofs, or algebrization-style obstacles apply.
tasks.rationale: Early barrier classification prevents repeated investment in proof schemas already known to be insufficient.
tasks.successCriteria: A checkable classification argument that identifies which barrier property is present or absent.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A sharply stated unanswered property whose resolution would decide whether the barrier applies.
tasks.verificationMethod: Compare the formalized schema with the definitions of each tested barrier, avoiding analogy-only conclusions.

tasks.title: Close one a priori estimate
tasks.objective: Choose one candidate a priori estimate for three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes, state the solution class and boundary conditions, and test whether every nonlinear term closes without assuming the desired regularity.
tasks.rationale: Circular use of smoothness is a frequent hidden defect in regularity arguments.
tasks.successCriteria: A closed estimate with constants and norms explicit in a nontrivial declared setting.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: The first term that cannot be controlled, together with the exact missing embedding or integrability bound.
tasks.verificationMethod: Re-derive each integration-by-parts and functional inequality step, including endpoint and boundary terms.

tasks.title: Normalize a continuation criterion
tasks.objective: Write one regularity or continuation criterion in a fully quantified form, map its dependencies, and identify the smallest new bound that would make it applicable to arbitrary admissible data.
tasks.rationale: A dependency-normalized criterion gives later attempts a precise target instead of an informal route.
tasks.successCriteria: A self-contained criterion statement and a proved implication from the named missing bound.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A specific quantifier, endpoint, or solution-class mismatch preventing the implication.
tasks.verificationMethod: Type-check all spaces, scaling exponents, and time intervals, then independently audit the implication.

tasks.title: Test closure of a structured blow-up ansatz
tasks.objective: Specify a finite- or sparse-mode divergence-free ansatz for three-dimensional Navier-Stokes and determine exactly whether the nonlinear evolution preserves it or generates forbidden modes.
tasks.rationale: An invariant ansatz can reduce the PDE, while a proved closure failure rules out a tempting duplicate path.
tasks.successCriteria: An exact closure calculation and a reduced evolution whose admissibility conditions are proved.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: The first generated mode or constraint that destroys closure, recorded as a reusable obstruction.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent symbolic convolution and divergence checks, with exact arithmetic for any finite-mode computation.

tasks.title: Design a rigorous breakdown certificate
tasks.objective: State a finite, checkable collection of bounds that would imply finite-time breakdown for admissible Navier-Stokes data, and prove the implication without treating numerical growth as singularity.
tasks.rationale: A certificate contract separates candidate generation from the analytic proof needed to establish breakdown.
tasks.successCriteria: A complete implication from explicitly certified inequalities to loss of the required regularity.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A precise compactness, continuation, or numerical-error gap that prevents certification.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent PDE proof audit and interval-certified verification requirements for every numerical premise.

tasks.title: Map one special-case proof boundary
tasks.objective: Choose a sharply defined class of smooth projective varieties, state the strongest Hodge-conjecture result available within that class, and isolate one theorem-sized extension step without claiming the general case.
tasks.rationale: Special-case boundaries reveal concrete geometric dependencies that can be assigned independently.
tasks.successCriteria: A dependency-complete reduction of the extension to one explicit lemma.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A specific invariant or construction showing why the extension mechanism stops.
tasks.verificationMethod: Check all hypotheses on the variety, coefficients, and cycle class map in the reconstructed argument.

tasks.title: Test one algebraic-cycle construction
tasks.objective: For a concrete restricted family, propose an algebraic-cycle construction for a stated rational Hodge class and verify its type, rationality, and cohomology class step by step.
tasks.rationale: Concrete constructions can expose exactly which part of algebraicity is missing.
tasks.successCriteria: A valid construction for the declared family with a checkable cycle-class computation.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A minimal dimension, codimension, or rationality obstruction to the proposed construction.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent cohomological degree and Hodge-type checks plus an explicit cycle-class calculation.

tasks.title: Specify a non-algebraicity certificate
tasks.objective: Define what finite or symbolic evidence would certify that a proposed rational Hodge class is not in the span of algebraic cycle classes for a concrete variety.
tasks.rationale: Candidate generation is only useful when non-algebraicity can be separated from failure to find a cycle.
tasks.successCriteria: A sound certificate criterion and a verification procedure for a nontrivial restricted setting.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A proof that the proposed invariant cannot distinguish algebraic from non-algebraic classes in that setting.
tasks.verificationMethod: Prove soundness of the criterion and test it on known algebraic classes as negative controls.

tasks.title: Audit one obstruction invariant
tasks.objective: Select one invariant proposed to obstruct algebraicity of a rational Hodge class, formalize its functorial properties, and test whether algebraic cycles necessarily vanish under it.
tasks.rationale: An obstruction is meaningful only after its soundness on all algebraic cycles in scope is proved.
tasks.successCriteria: A sound vanishing theorem for the declared class of algebraic cycles.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A concrete algebraic cycle on which the invariant does not vanish.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent functoriality and cycle-class computations in explicit test cases.

tasks.title: Normalize a rank-one dependency chain
tasks.objective: Reconstruct one rank-zero or rank-one Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer implication as a dependency graph, state every local and global hypothesis, and isolate one independently checkable missing extension.
tasks.rationale: Known cases provide a calibrated base for identifying where higher-rank arguments actually need new ideas.
tasks.successCriteria: A complete implication graph with one precisely stated extension lemma.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A hypothesis mismatch or circular dependency that invalidates the proposed extension.
tasks.verificationMethod: Trace each implication back to its stated hypotheses and check all rank and finiteness assumptions.

tasks.title: Check one local-global compatibility step
tasks.objective: Select one local factor or descent datum used in a Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer argument, define its normalization explicitly, and prove its compatibility with the global rank or leading-term statement in a restricted case.
tasks.rationale: Normalization mismatches can silently break otherwise plausible rank comparisons.
tasks.successCriteria: A complete compatibility proof in the declared restricted case.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A concrete normalization, bad-reduction, or finiteness condition that blocks the comparison.
tasks.verificationMethod: Exact arithmetic on a small documented example plus an independent symbolic derivation.

tasks.title: Design an exact rank-mismatch certificate
tasks.objective: Specify the exact evidence required to certify both the analytic and algebraic rank of one elliptic curve strongly enough that a mismatch would be a genuine counterexample candidate.
tasks.rationale: Numerical rank heuristics alone cannot establish the claimed mismatch.
tasks.successCriteria: A sound two-sided certificate contract with explicit precision, descent, and finiteness requirements.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A precise reason one side cannot currently be certified for the proposed family.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent checking of the analytic error bound and algebraic rank bounds on control curves.

tasks.title: Prove a safe curve-family pruning rule
tasks.objective: For a precisely bounded elliptic-curve family, derive one exact rule that removes curves already incapable of yielding a certifiable rank mismatch, while preserving every possible counterexample in scope.
tasks.rationale: Safe pruning turns repeated finite searches into reusable infrastructure.
tasks.successCriteria: A proved pruning criterion and reproducible exact checker.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A smallest curve showing the proposed pruning criterion is unsound.
tasks.verificationMethod: Exact arithmetic tests against exhaustive small controls and an independent proof of preservation.

tasks.title: Isolate one continuum-limit bridge
tasks.objective: State one theorem-sized implication from a regulated or lattice Yang-Mills construction toward a four-dimensional continuum theory, including the exact uniform bounds and axioms required.
tasks.rationale: Finite-regulator evidence does not settle the problem unless the continuum passage is rigorous.
tasks.successCriteria: A proved restricted implication or a complete reduction to one explicit uniform estimate.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A precise loss of compactness, gauge control, or uniformity that blocks the limit.
tasks.verificationMethod: Audit every regulator-dependent constant and every limit interchange against the stated axioms.

tasks.title: Formalize one mass-gap implication
tasks.objective: Choose one precise correlation-decay or spectral statement and prove, under explicitly stated axioms, the implication needed to obtain a positive mass gap.
tasks.rationale: Translating physics intuition into a checkable implication creates a reusable target for construction attempts.
tasks.successCriteria: A complete implication with the Hilbert-space, positivity, and spectral hypotheses explicit.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A missing axiom or countermodel showing the proposed implication is too strong.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent functional-analytic derivation and hypothesis-by-hypothesis countermodel search.

tasks.title: Stress-test one construction axiom set
tasks.objective: Take one proposed continuum Yang-Mills construction framework, state a minimal subset of its axioms, and search for a rigorous incompatibility or a model demonstrating their consistency at that level.
tasks.rationale: A precise obstruction to an intermediate framework is useful even when it does not refute the prize statement.
tasks.successCriteria: A proved incompatibility among the declared assumptions, clearly labeled as an intermediate obstruction.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A concrete model satisfying the tested subset, ruling out that attempted obstruction.
tasks.verificationMethod: Formal implication checking and explicit model verification.

tasks.title: Audit a gapless candidate's admissibility
tasks.objective: Specify one proposed gapless behavior and test, one axiom at a time, whether it belongs to the exact four-dimensional quantum Yang-Mills setting required by the problem.
tasks.rationale: A gapless example outside the required axiomatic setting is not a counterexample.
tasks.successCriteria: A fully admissible gapless candidate reduction with all remaining proof obligations explicit.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: The first required axiom, dimension, gauge, or continuum condition the candidate violates.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent axiom checklist and dimensional and spectral consistency checks.

tasks.title: Reconstruct a proof dependency slice
tasks.objective: Select one bounded segment of the Ricci-flow-with-surgery proof of the Poincare Conjecture, state its inputs and outputs precisely, and reconstruct the dependency chain without skipping analytic hypotheses.
tasks.rationale: The solved track calibrates whether the protocol preserves real proof structure rather than plausible summaries.
tasks.successCriteria: A faithful dependency-aware reconstruction whose claims can be checked against established sources.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A precisely identified missing theorem or hypothesis in the reconstruction.
tasks.verificationMethod: Compare every dependency and conclusion with an established proof exposition and record discrepancies.

tasks.title: Formalize one settled lemma interface
tasks.objective: Choose one theorem-sized lemma from the established Poincare proof, translate its statement into a dependency-explicit formal interface, and identify every definition still preventing machine checking.
tasks.rationale: A known-correct track exposes ambiguity and schema failures before they affect open-problem claims.
tasks.successCriteria: A well-typed formal statement and a complete list of imported lemmas or a checked proof in a restricted setting.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A minimal ambiguity in the source statement that blocks faithful formalization.
tasks.verificationMethod: Type checking where available and independent comparison with the established theorem statement.

tasks.title: Resolve one adversarial objection
tasks.objective: Formulate the strongest precise objection to one bounded step of an established Poincare proof, then trace whether the literature's hypotheses and lemmas resolve it.
tasks.rationale: A solved result provides ground truth for measuring whether generated critiques distinguish genuine gaps from answered objections.
tasks.successCriteria: A sourced resolution or a precisely scoped unresolved exposition gap without challenging the accepted theorem beyond the evidence.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A demonstration that the objection was ill-posed, with the missing definition or hypothesis identified.
tasks.verificationMethod: Independent source tracing and line-by-line comparison of the objection with the lemma actually used.

tasks.title: Calibrate the claim-review checklist
tasks.objective: Apply the Millennium claim and evidence checklist to one established Poincare proof fragment, record false positives and missed dependencies, and propose one concrete review-rule improvement.
tasks.rationale: Review tooling should be calibrated against known mathematics before it grades novel attempts.
tasks.successCriteria: A reproducible checklist evaluation and one justified protocol improvement.
tasks.usefulFailureCriteria: A documented reason the checklist cannot express a required proof dependency.
tasks.verificationMethod: A second independent checklist pass and comparison with an established exposition.
